def generate()->bytes:
    # Try to craft a NetBIOS packet that triggers terminate trace dissection with
    # extra bytes after NB_SIGNATURE so tvb_offset_exists() keeps returning true.
    # We don't know exact framing; produce a large blob with plausible fields.
    # Put flag with 0x80 set at presumed NB_DATA1 offset.
    data = bytearray(b"\x00"*512)
    # Heuristic: set many bytes to nonzero so dissector continues.
    for i in range(len(data)):
        data[i] = (i*7) & 0xff
    # Ensure flag byte somewhere early is 0x80.
    data[1] = 0x80
    return bytes(data)

full_messages.content:
You are a vulnerability verifier. All candidate functions are already
reachable from the fuzzer — do NOT re-litigate reachability as pass/fail. Your job
is to gather EVIDENCE about whether the reached code actually contains a
crashing memory-safety bug of the stated type, then submit it.

Gather evidence with the tools:
- read_function(name): read the real source.
- check_reachability(function_name): confirm the call graph (depth, direct/indirect).
- reach_probe(generator_code, target): write Python `def generate()->bytes` that
  produces an input aiming to REACH `target` (a function name or "file.c:LINE").
  It runs the input on the real ASan binary under gdb and tells you whether the
  target was reached and whether it crashed. A crash is proof; a reach grounds
  your judgment. Only a real crash or reach can raise the score above the ceiling —
  you cannot assert a high score from reading alone.
- submit_evidence(...): report your structured findings (see its schema). Call it
  once, last.

Two of the fields are NOT about scoring — they correct the SP for the downstream
PoV stage, and you are the right one to write them because you just read the real
code (and maybe ran a reach_probe):
- corrected_description: if the SP's stated bug type/description is wrong or
  imprecise given the real code, write the accurate one (else restate it).
- control_flow_to_bug: the real path from the fuzzer entry to the crash site — the
  key functions, branches, and conditions that must hold to trigger it.

Do NOT pass things "when in doubt". Report what the evidence shows. Absence of a
crash is not proof of safety; a proven clamp/guard on the tainted value IS
disconfirming.

Verify this suspicious point.

Fuzzer: handler_netbios   Sanitizer: address
Function: dissect_netb_terminate_trace
Claimed bug type: heap-buffer-overflow
Suspicious-point description (from the finder — may be imprecise): Potential heap buffer overflow (ASan-detectable) in signature hex-string construction. Function allocates `signature` as `g_malloc(NB_SIZE_HMAC + 1)` or `g_malloc(NB_SIZE_TMAC + 1)` depending on a flag, then enters a loop that appends two hex characters per input byte via `signature[index++] = ...` twice per iteration while `tvb_offset_exists()` remains true. There is no bounds check that `index + 2` stays within the allocated size, so if the loop processes more bytes than expected (e.g., tvb contains more signature bytes than NB_SIZE_*), `index` can exceed the allocation, causing out-of-bounds write and later OOB write at the null terminator `signature[index] = '\0'`.

Control flow: allocate signature buffer based on flag -> loop over tvb bytes while offset exists -> write two chars per byte to signature with post-increment index -> write NUL terminator -> free.

Related: NB_SIZE_HMAC, NB_SIZE_TMAC, tvb_offset_exists(), index variable, signature buffer allocation size, loop termination condition based on tvb length rather than NB_SIZE_*.

The function is reachable (confirm with check_reachability if useful).

Read the function, judge whether a fuzzer input can drive a heap-buffer-overflow
there, optionally reach_probe a candidate input to ground it, then submit_evidence.

finder_sp_description:
Potential heap buffer overflow (ASan-detectable) in signature hex-string construction. Function allocates `signature` as `g_malloc(NB_SIZE_HMAC + 1)` or `g_malloc(NB_SIZE_TMAC + 1)` depending on a flag, then enters a loop that appends two hex characters per input byte via `signature[index++] = ...` twice per iteration while `tvb_offset_exists()` remains true. There is no bounds check that `index + 2` stays within the allocated size, so if the loop processes more bytes than expected (e.g., tvb contains more signature bytes than NB_SIZE_*), `index` can exceed the allocation, causing out-of-bounds write and later OOB write at the null terminator `signature[index] = '\0'`.

Control flow: allocate signature buffer based on flag -> loop over tvb bytes while offset exists -> write two chars per byte to signature with post-increment index -> write NUL terminator -> free.

Related: NB_SIZE_HMAC, NB_SIZE_TMAC, tvb_offset_exists(), index variable, signature buffer allocation size, loop termination condition based on tvb length rather than NB_SIZE_*.
